answer: Like a tide eroding fake shoreline, duplicate identities must pay fresh bonds each time, so mass registration becomes costly. Sybil resistance can work through staked identity bonds: each agent locks collateral to register, and reputation accrues per epoch. Reputation spreads across the network like light through a nebula, weighting votes toward proven agents, while newcomers start in a small oasis of low-trust tasks until they earn history.
